text:
alex_k: quick sync — ran a kernel-selection + microbatch sizing experiment on the pink pool earlier today. p95 looks fine but p99 jumped ~2.2x on a small slice of traffic (long-context user queries). sharing notes and a short profile dump. :eyes:

jia_w: can you paste the numbers and the exact config? microbatch size + kernel flags?

alex_k: test config: microbatch_target=24 -> control=8, kernel_pref='fast-attn-v2', fallback='safe-attn', kv_policy=LRU-evict-oldest, seq_threshold=2048. Workload: 6k requests, 2.1% > 1500 tokens input. Results: p50 40ms (same), p95 95ms (same), p99 1.6s -> 3.5s on the experiment. tail count small but visible.

samir_r: that smells like kernel fallback serialization + KV cache churn. when the fast kernel handles short seqs concurrently but long seqs force fallback and block GPU warps -> microbatch waits. did you capture kernel fallback rate?

alex_k: pasted a trimmed profiler snippet: 
```
TRACE 1793254321
requests: 6000
microbatch_target:24
fallback_count: 112
fallback_serialization_events: 76
avg_kv_evictions/sec: 220
avg_kv_hits: 87%
latency_ms: p50=40 p95=95 p99=3500
long_input_percent>1500: 2.1%
samples_with_kv_miss_at_tail: 84
```

ben_p: do we know whether KV eviction is evicting prefixes or recently used tokens? LRU evict-oldest might remove prefix tokens that would have helped next tokens -> more recompute. If eviction correlates with fallback_count that's bad.

alex_k: eviction logs show most evictions are oldest prefixes when burst of long seqs hit. KV size limit configured for 24k keys. When microbatch grows, requests aggregate, more keys allocated, triggers eviction spikes.

jia_w: two levers that look promising: (A) keep microbatch_target small for pools with heavy long-tail (eg target=8-12), or (B) add an early truncation gate to requests that are likely to push fallback/kvcache churn. Also we can reduce seq_threshold for the aggressive kernel so we avoid attempted fast kernel on borderline long sequences.

marie_ops: ops question: what SLO guard do we need? current SLO is 95th < 120ms and 99th < 1s for this tier. experiment breached p99 badly. we should apply a conservative timeout to protect downstream callers. my vote: 6s request timeout + soft max_tokens cap on hosted tier while we iterate.

ben_p: propose pragmatic short-term policy:
- request_timeout: 7s (hard)
- soft_max_tokens: 512 default for public hosted (overrideable by customer explicit opt-in)
- microbatch_target: 12 for pink pool
- kernel_seq_threshold: reduce from 2048 -> 1536 so fast-attn-v2 doesn't try to handle very long sequences that it falls back on for

This should reduce fallback_serialization events and lower KV churn.

jia_w: long-term we should implement adaptive truncation heuristics: if (input_len + expected_gen) > k limit -> trim prefix using a scoring heuristic (drop low-attention paragraphs first). Pseudocode: 
```
if input_len + est_gen > MAX_SEQ:
  prune = select_prefix_to_trim(input, budget=input_len + est_gen - MAX_SEQ)
  input = trim_prefix(input, prune)
```
Also record a metric truncated_ratio and set an alert if truncation_rate > 0.5% per 10m.

samir_r: agree on the heuristics. also add kernel-fallback telemetry: count where fallback caused >1s stall and emit trace sampling. For immediate mitigation we can also route long sequence requests to a slower but stable kernel path or to a smaller model instance (model_fallback_route) instead of letting fallback happen inline. That avoids blocking the microbatch.

alex_k: noted. small implementation plan: 1) revert pink pool to microbatch_target=12 and kernel_seq_threshold=1536 (hotfix), 2) apply soft_max_tokens=512 on hosted by default, 3) add fallback telemetry + trace sampling. I'll open follow-ups.

ci-bot: perf-collector: created trace ticket PERF-2028 for sampled p99 traces (see /perf/trace/2028) :robot_face:

marie_ops: new action: put an emergency runbook change — if p99 > 1.5s for 3m, auto-scale down microbatch target by 50% and enable per-route max_tokens 256. We can iterate after observing.

ben_p: small note: if we add soft_max_tokens, ensure client SDKs get a clear 4xx-ish structured error when we truncate so apps can surface that to users gracefully. maybe return a header X-Redwood-Truncated: true and a warning body.

jia_w: good call. Also instrument KV eviction events and tie them to request ids so we can correlate which inputs caused rework.

alex_k: thanks all — I'll land the hotfix changes on pink and run a 10k request smoke in the morning, will post updated p95/p99. assigning: samir -> kernel fallback telemetry change, ben -> SDK truncation header, jia -> adaptive truncation prototype, marie -> runbook entry.

marie_ops: ack :thumbsup: 

alex_k: fyi will tag this under PERF-2028 and follow up in 24h with numbers.
